name: Perimeter — Host Exhibiting Multiple Attack Behaviors (Confirmed Compromise)
description:
Attacker objective
A fully-compromised internal host progressing through the kill chain — combining beaconing/C2, scanning, sweep, lateral movement, or internal exploitation.

Attack logic
Any single perimeter detection can be an isolated event. A host that triggers two or more distinct perimeter detections within a short window is exhibiting a multi-stage attack pattern.

Why this detection works
Correlating the count of distinct detection types per host over the alert stream converts several weak or medium signals into one high-confidence compromise alert.

False positives
Very low — requires two independent behaviours on the same host; a benign scanner plus a monitoring host could co-trigger.

Tuning
Exclude verified infrastructure that legitimately trips multiple behaviours.

Required telemetry
The perimeter detection alerts produced by the FortiGate/PAN-OS rules (host/source.ip and rule name present in the alert stream).
author: raadabujaish
note:
## Investigation guide
1. source.ip = the compromised host; the correlated list shows which behaviours it exhibited (e.g. beaconing + lateral).
2. This is a confirmed-compromise pattern — isolate the host and begin IR immediately.
false_positives: Very low — requires two independent behaviours on the same host; a benign scanner plus a monitoring host could co-trigger.
query: FROM .alerts-security.alerts-* METADATA _id, _index, _version | WHERE source.ip IS NOT NULL AND kibana.alert.rule.name LIKE "FortiGate*" | STATS distinct_detections = COUNT_DISTINCT(kibana.alert.rule.name), detections = VALUES(kibana.alert.rule.name) BY source.ip | WHERE distinct_detections >= 2
